      <title>Newcastle United v Everton: Premier League – live</title>
      <link>https://www.theguardian.com/football/live/2026/nov/02/newcastle-united-v-everton-premier-league-live</link>
      <description><ul><li><p>Premier League updates from the 8pm GMT kick-off</p></li><li><p><a href="https://www.theguardian.com/football/live">Live scores</a> | <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/football/2026/nov/02/football-daily-email-aston-villa">Read today’s Football Daily</a> | <a href="mailto:Daniel.Harris@theguardian.com">Email Daniel</a></p></li></ul><p><strong>Everton, meanwhile, wo’t be afraid to go long, with Barry contesting aerial balls and Rohl, Dewsbury-Hall and George looking to get </strong><em><strong>in and around</strong> </em><strong>him. </strong>George, in particular, will be tasked with running at the newcastle defenders, while Dewsbury-Hall will look to prompt around the box, nudging balls in behind or shooting, and box-crash with make third-man runs. Otherwise, Barry will look to run off the centre-backs, who don’t have the pace to keep up, and look for one-touch close-range finishes.</p><p><strong>So where is the game? </strong>Newcastle will, I think, look to defend pretty deep, partly because the lack pace at the back, but also because they want to create space to counter. Elanga is brilliant on the break, but Barnes can also run, likewise Willock, whose eye for a goal is excellent. I also think they’ll want Gonzalez to control the play, with Joelinton often ahead of the ball looking to win high turnovers – they’ll reckon he has the physicality to get after Garner – and also send their full-backs forward so the wingers can attack the box, with crosses and cut-backs directed at Osula.</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/football/live/2026/nov/02/newcastle-united-v-everton-premier-league-live">Continue reading...</a></description>

But given the team in second are Manchester City, who are likely to be facing at the very least a <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/football/2026/sep/25/manchester-city-abu-dhabi-era-trophies-transfers-and-charges">major points deduction</a>, perhaps more significant is that they are five clear of Brighton in third.       <title>‘We had to dig in’: Arsenal’s Anfield win was performance of champions, says Rice</title>
      <link>https://www.theguardian.com/football/2026/nov/02/arsenal-liverpool-declan-rice-champions</link>
      <description><ul><li><p>Midfielder praises his side’s grit and determination</p></li><li><p>Szoboszlai says there are fine margins between teams</p></li></ul><p>Declan Rice says Arsenal are ready for more grinding wins as he hailed <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/football/2026/nov/01/liverpool-arsenal-premier-league-match-report">the 1-0 success at Liverpool</a> on Sunday as the performance of champions. The midfielder set up Kai Havertz for the only goal on 16 minutes but his physicality and reading of the game on the defensive side were arguably more impressive.</p><p><a href="https://www.theguardian.com/football/2026/nov/01/andoni-iraola-responds-liverpool-penalty-denial-arsenal-premier-league">Liverpool were unhappy at the non-award of a penalty</a> for a Jurriën Timber shirt-pull on Alexander Isak in the 21st minute and it was a day when the Kop fumed about Arsenal’s streetwise tactics, especially how they won free-kicks – albeit their own players were also guilty of going down too easily at times. The Arsenal goalkeeper David Raya was booked for time-wasting in the 92nd minute as his team closed out the victory.</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/football/2026/nov/02/arsenal-liverpool-declan-rice-champions">Continue reading...</a></description>

      <title>Premier League: 10 talking points from the weekend’s action</title>
      <link>https://www.theguardian.com/football/2026/nov/02/premier-league-10-talking-points-from-the-weekends-action</link>
      <description><p>Marco Rose’s tactics are lifting Bournemouth, Roméo Lavia makes progress with Chelsea and Roberto De Zerbi gives youth a chance at Spurs</p><p>Good defending is the mark of champions. At Anfield, where Arsenal had not won in the past 13 visits, Mikel Arteta followed the orthodoxy of locking down once his team took the lead. This time around, it proved successful. Arsenal did not allow the occasion or the stadium to get to them as they have on previous occasions. In April 2023, Granit Xhaka entangling with Trent Alexander-Arnold energised home fans previously despondent that Arsenal were 2-0 up. It finished 2-2. On Sunday, Liverpool zipped around zestfully, as Andoni Iraola requests, though the final-ball quality was lacking. That owed a great deal to the organisation of the Arsenal defence. Ahead of the last international break, Brighton set a blueprint for getting the better of Arsenal in <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/football/2026/sep/19/brighton-arsenal-premier-league-match-report">winning 3-0</a>. Liverpool’s squad profile might have made a similar strategy possible though Iraola’s outfit is struggling to create chances in the same volume as Brighton or his Bournemouth team. <strong>John Brewin</strong></p><p><em>Match report: <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/football/2026/nov/01/liverpool-arsenal-premier-league-match-report">Liverpool 0-1 Arsenal</a></em></p><p><em>Reaction:</em> <em><a href="https://www.theguardian.com/football/2026/nov/01/andoni-iraola-responds-liverpool-penalty-denial-arsenal-premier-league">Iraola responds to Isak penalty denial</a></em></p><p><em>Match report: <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/football/2026/oct/31/aston-villa-fulham-premier-league-match-report">Aston Villa 1-1 Fulham</a></em></p><p><em>Match report: <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/football/2026/oct/31/bournemouth-leeds-premier-league-match-report">Bournemouth 2-0 Leeds United</a></em></p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/football/2026/nov/02/premier-league-10-talking-points-from-the-weekends-action">Continue reading...</a></description>

      <title>‘We have to tell them to go down’: Iraola responds to Isak penalty denial for Liverpool</title>
      <link>https://www.theguardian.com/football/2026/nov/01/andoni-iraola-responds-liverpool-penalty-denial-arsenal-premier-league</link>
      <description><ul><li><p>Manager rues two dismissed penalty claims by referee</p></li><li><p>Iraola complains ‘if you don’t go down, you don’t call it’</p></li></ul><p>Andoni Iraola said he will instruct Liverpool players to go down in the box in future after Alexander Isak was denied a penalty during Arsenal’s first win at Anfield for 14 years.</p><p>Liverpool were beaten by <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/football/2026/nov/01/liverpool-arsenal-premier-league-match-report">Kai Havertz’s early strike</a> after a poor clearance from the goalkeeper ­Alisson but had two penalty claims dismissed by the referee, Andy Madley. The first, a shirt-pull by the Arsenal defender Jurriën Timber on Isak, prevented the ­Sweden international reaching Bradley Barcola’s cross. The second, a hold by Christos ­Tzolis on Cody Gakpo, was reviewed by the video assistant referee, Stuart Attwell, but rejected.</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/football/2026/nov/01/andoni-iraola-responds-liverpool-penalty-denial-arsenal-premier-league">Continue reading...</a></description>
